questions.question: The bookstore bot's answers keep coming back as long paragraphs instead of short bullet lists. Fix?
questions.explanation: Show two short examples in the target format; examples steer format more reliably than emphasis.

questions.question: The bot tells a customer signed first editions can be returned within 60 days. The policy doesn't mention them. Fix?
questions.answer: Put the policy text in context and tell it to answer only from it.
questions.explanation: Grounding the answer in the text you provide is the first defence against invented rules.

questions.concept: Order and delimiters in the context
questions.question: Where do you put the five-paragraph returns policy: in the system prompt or in the customer's message?
questions.explanation: Keep the rules and the policy in the system prompt, the policy in its own delimited block; order and delimiters change how the model reads it.

questions.question: What's a sign your system prompt is too long?
questions.answer: Rules contradict each other and nobody tests them.
questions.explanation: Untested rules pile up; test cases (and later evals) keep a prompt honest.

questions.question: Context window vs max_tokens again: which one caps the length of the bot's answer?
questions.explanation: max_tokens limits the answer; the window limits input and answer together.

questions.question: All three of your examples end with "Happy reading!". What happens?
questions.answer: Most answers will end that way too.
questions.explanation: The model copies patterns in examples, including the ones you didn't mean.

questions.question: The instruction says "no closing line", the examples have one. Which wins?
questions.explanation: When instructions and examples disagree, examples tend to win.
